**My thinking this season**

Well, I'm 68 now, been doing this for 50 years, and I've got my six mu of stevia to think about. My son works off-farm in the county town, so it's mostly me and my wife now. The older I get, the more I hire help for the heavy work — my back isn't what it used to be.

Stevia is a picky crop, but I've grown it long enough to know what it wants. The soil on my plot is decent loam, not too sandy. I had a fair yield last year, about 220 kg of dried leaf per mu, which is respectable for this area. The buyer paid 12 yuan per kg, so I cleared enough to cover inputs and have a bit left. I'm not rich, but I know this crop.

**Planting:** I'll transplant stevia seedlings around April 20th. I start them in my small nursery bed in late March — I've been doing this myself for years. With 6 mu, I need about 8,000 seedlings per mu, so roughly 48,000 seedlings total. I buy the improved stevia variety "Zhongsitian No. 1" seeds — about 0.15 kg of seed for the nursery, costs me around 200 yuan total. The nursery takes some labor but it's worth it.

**Fertilizer:** Stevia needs nitrogen, but too much and the leaves get thin and the stevioside content drops. Based on my soil and last year's results, I'll apply about 18 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base fertilizer before transplanting — that's about 108 kg total, costing roughly 350 yuan. Then I'll topdress twice: once at about 40 days after planting with 8 kg urea per mu, and again at flowering stage with another 5 kg urea per mu. I also add about 500 kg of well-rotted manure per mu — I have two mu worth from my own livestock, and I'll buy the rest from my neighbor for about 300 yuan. Total N works out to roughly 12 kg per mu, P₂O₅ about 5 kg per mu, K₂O about 5 kg per mu. I've learned over the years that stevia doesn't need as much N as maize — quality matters more than bulk leaf.

**Irrigation:** I'll irrigate four times this year. First, right after transplanting to help the seedlings settle. Second at the rapid growth stage in June. Third in July if it gets dry — last July was scorching and I regretted not watering a fourth time. Fourth in August before the final growth push. Pumping costs about 40 yuan per mu per irrigation, so 4 × 6 × 40 = 960 yuan. Water is getting expensive but stevia wilts badly without it.

**Pesticide:** I'll spray herbicide once before transplanting — glyphosate to clean the weeds, about 30 yuan per mu. Then I'll watch for aphids; they love stevia. If I see them, I'll spray imidacloprid once, maybe twice. I also watch for leaf spot disease in humid August weather. I budget about 80 yuan per mu for pesticides.

**Labor:** My wife and I can handle the daily tending, transplanting, and harvesting with some hired help. I figure 25 family days between us for the season, and I'll hire 12 days of labor — mostly for transplanting and harvesting. Hired labor is 120 yuan per day now. That's 1,440 yuan.

**Tillage:** I'll plow once with the small tiller I own, then harrow and make ridges. My nephew helps with the tilling when his schedule allows. After harvest, I'll leave the stubble and till in manure for next spring.

**Yield expectation:** If the weather cooperates and I irrigate well, I expect about 230 kg dried leaf per mu. Last year was dry and I only got 220, but I'm being a bit optimistic because I'm planning that extra irrigation. 230 kg × 6 mu = 1,380 kg total. At 12 yuan/kg, that's 16,560 yuan gross. After inputs and labor, I should clear around 11,000-12,000 yuan. It's modest but steady. At my age, I value steady over risky.
